sources.title: Cats Protection: Cats hiding
sources.method: Web reader; main hiding and refuge sections read
facts: Hiding can be part of ordinary cat behaviour, including sleep, security and play.
Provide quiet, undisturbed, covered retreats, raised when suitable, away from food, water and litter.
Respect the cat's choice to stay hidden rather than coaxing a stressed cat out.
Hiding more than usual warrants veterinary advice; a retreat is not a diagnosis or substitute for checking a change.

sources.title: Cats Protection: Shy cats
sources.method: Web reader; sections on hiding, routine and interaction read
facts: Do not force interaction; let a shy cat approach.
Friends and family should not seek the cat out inside its hiding place.
Maintaining routines and quietly sharing space without forcing attention are recommended in the specific context of shy cats; not evidence for a universal workday schedule.

sources.title: Cats Protection: Cats and play
sources.method: Web reader; main play, toy supervision and routine sections read
facts: Play may include stalking, pouncing, chasing and batting.
Wand toys can imitate prey; allow occasional catches.
Short games can be appropriate, rotate toys, supervise entangling or shreddable toys and inspect wear.
Do not use fingers or toes as play targets.
No universal play-duration prescription or diagnosis of a laptop interruption is inferred.
